Senses.Explanation: To select the milk is to distinguish what matters within a mixture whose parts are not obvious at a glance. Chan masters make it the goose king’s capacity: unlike ducks, it selects milk from water, and the image becomes a verdict on whether someone can tell the live point of an encounter from its similar-looking alternatives. Wansong Xingxiu states the image most explicitly: selecting milk from water requires the goose king. He applies it to the fine discrimination needed to read how the participants handle a case. Guishan Lingyou calls Yangshan’s raised ear of grain “the goose king selecting milk” after Yangshan refuses a choice among green, yellow, and neither. The act distinguishes the point without accepting the offered alternatives. Dahui repeatedly uses the formula as a verdict. He applies it to Yangshan’s apparently contradictory statements about awakening, to two identical-looking offerings treated differently, and to the precise shortfall in Baofu’s answer. The goose-versus-duck contrast does not make the phrase a claim about birds or a general compliment for intelligence. In these records it names discrimination demonstrated in a concrete exchange, and Dahui adds that it requires seeing with one’s own eyes.
